card: Batches block file pruning into a single pass over the block index rather than traversing the full index once per pruned file. When starting a node with pruning enabled on an existing full-chain datadir or pruning thousands of files at once, the previous O(M * N) approach executed billions of iterations while holding cs_main, freezing the node for tens of seconds on desktop hardware and up to 10 minutes on a Raspberry Pi 5. Benchmarks on ~972k blocks and 5,770 files report reducing pruning time from 606s to 26ms on ARM64 and 75s to 15ms on x86_64.
changed_since_previous: Added upfront range validation using set bounds to throw `std::out_of_range` before any index entries are modified, updated test fixture setup to parse block manager arguments, and added unit tests covering batch pruning, out-of-range error handling, dirty-index tracking, and the manual pruning path.
evidence: Author benchmark on ~972k blocks and 5,770 files to prune: x86_64 startup time dropped from 75.1s to 14.7ms (~5,100x), and Raspberry Pi 5 dropped from 606.0s to 26.3ms (>3,500x).

Author explanation in description: 'When pruning a full chain (~5,770 files and ~972k blocks), this triggered ~5.6 billion iterations and froze the node running on a Pi 5 for ~10 minutes on startup while holding cs_main.'
problem: Switching a node with full chain history to pruned mode, or manually pruning a large backlog of block files, iterated over the entire `m_block_index` separately for each pruned file. On a full chain (~5,770 files and ~972k blocks), this O(M * N) loop performed ~5.6 billion iterations while holding `cs_main`, freezing the node for tens of seconds on x86_64 and up to 10 minutes on a Raspberry Pi on startup.

risk.why: A bug in batch pruning could improperly clear block data status on unpruned blocks or fail to prune files, corrupting the in-memory block index or leading to crashes when accessing pruned data.

summary: Replaces `PruneOneBlockFile` with `PruneBlockFiles(const std::set<int>&)` in `BlockManager`, batching block file pruning into a single pass over `m_block_index` using a dynamic bitfield. In `FindFilesToPrune` and `FindFilesToPruneManual`, candidate files are aggregated and pruned together rather than traversing the full block index once per file. It also skips block index entries that lack both block and undo data, preventing header-only or already-pruned entries from being dirtied when file 0 is pruned, and validates file numbers up front to reject out-of-range inputs before modifying the index.
